commands.purpose: Execute auto-LiRPA capability probe on native 1D and singleton-height 2D surrogate

requirement_evidence.notes: Extracted installed metadata for Python 3.11, PyTorch 2.14.1+cpu, and auto-LiRPA 0.8.0, identifying version contract violation.
Pinned requirements and lock specification for the isolated verifier environment without mutating .venv.
Native 1D graph conversion failed due to auto-LiRPA pooling.py IndexError in pads attribute; full traceback captured.
Mapped Conv1d, BatchNorm1d, MaxPool1d, ReLU, Flatten, and Linear attributes into 2D singleton-height equivalent.
Sampled logits max abs diff is 0.0, but IEEE-754 universal float32 equivalence across BLAS routines remains unproven.
Separated conversion setup time (21.6ms) from per-build bound times (IBP: ~3-8ms, CROWN: ~427-1661ms).
Reported outcomes separately: Native 1D FAILED (zero synthetic bounds), 2D surrogate CONDITIONAL_DIAGNOSTIC.

scientific_dispositions.evidence: auto-LiRPA fails natively on 1D convolution/pooling graphs due to assumptions in operator pads indexing. 2D surrogate is mathematically equivalent in R but unproven in IEEE-754.
CROWN per-bound runtime (~427ms) exceeds the streaming deadline (20ms) by more than 20x, confirming unviability for real-time per-window certified inference.
Version contract mismatch: auto-LiRPA 0.8.0 requires torch<2.12.0 whereas runtime uses torch 2.14.1+cpu.

limitations: Native 1D auto-LiRPA bound execution is completely unsupported without monkey-patching or third-party library source modifications.
2D surrogate bounds are diagnostic only and cannot be used as formal execution certificates for the 1D frozen reference.
